Architect.summary: Design buildings and spaces by combining creativity, math, technology, codes and collaboration.
steps: Explore an accredited architecture degree or another approved route toward professional licensure.
Job-shadow, intern, build a portfolio, and seek design/engineering exposure.
Complete required professional experience and licensing examinations for the state where you plan to practice.
Join a design firm, specialize, or eventually create your own practice.

Electrician.summary: Install, troubleshoot and maintain electrical systems in homes, businesses, industry and new construction.
steps: Apply for a registered apprenticeship or employer/union training route combining paid work and classroom instruction.
Complete required hours and state examinations for the appropriate electrical credential.
Build residential, commercial or industrial troubleshooting, code and customer-service skills.
With experience and proper licensing, explore estimating, insurance, accounting and owning a company.

Registered Nurse.summary: Provide direct patient care, coordinate treatment, and educate patients and families.
steps: Complete an approved ADN or BSN nursing program.
Complete supervised clinical rotations in approved healthcare settings.
Pass the NCLEX-RN and satisfy state licensing requirements.
Work in hospitals, clinics, schools, community health or a specialty area.

Veterinarian.summary: Diagnose and treat animals while advising owners about health, prevention and care.
steps: Complete college prerequisites and gain animal/veterinary experience.
Complete an accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine program.
Complete applicable national and state licensing requirements.
Work in a clinic, specialty practice, public health, research or eventually own a practice.

Software Developer.summary: Design and build software, websites, apps and digital systems.
steps: Programming fundamentals, Git, web development, databases and problem solving.
Compare computer science, software engineering, IT, community college, certificates or validated training routes.
Build real projects, internships, hackathons or open-source work.
Apply for junior developer roles, apprenticeships or internships and keep building a portfolio.

Teacher.summary: Help students learn, grow and build skills in a classroom or specialized educational setting.
steps: Complete an approved educator-preparation program and degree appropriate to the intended subject/grade level.
Complete supervised field experiences and student teaching.
Meet state educator certification requirements for the intended endorsement.
Apply to districts, continue professional learning and consider additional endorsements.

Firefighter.summary: Respond to fires, medical emergencies, rescues and community safety needs.
steps: EMT training is commonly valuable or required depending on department.
Meet department testing, background, medical and physical ability standards.
Advance through experience, EMS/fire certifications and specialty training.

Police Officer.summary: Protect the community, respond to emergencies, investigate incidents and work with residents.
steps: Explore criminal justice, public safety, military service or community-college pathways if useful.
Meet agency age, education, background, medical, physical and examination requirements.
Complete an approved police academy and field training.
Develop expertise in community policing, investigations, youth services or leadership.

TV News Reporter / Local Anchor.summary: Research, report and explain news stories clearly on camera and across digital platforms.
steps: Explore journalism, communications, broadcasting, political science or a related field.
Work on school media, podcasts or video projects; learn interviewing, editing and fact-checking.
Seek newsroom, local-TV, radio, digital-media or communications internships.
Build an on-air/digital portfolio and begin in reporting, production or multimedia journalism.

Broadway Director / Actor.summary: Build a professional life in theatre through acting, directing, auditions, rehearsal and production experience.
steps: Consider BFA/BA theatre programs, conservatory study, workshops, voice, movement and directing training.
Develop headshots, résumé, reels, directing materials and a record of productions.
Audition, assist directors, join productions, pursue internships and build professional relationships.
Pursue regional theatre, touring and New York opportunities; understand representation and union pathways.

Chef / Restaurant Owner.summary: Create food, lead kitchen teams and potentially build a restaurant or food business.
steps: Choose culinary school, community college or direct kitchen apprenticeship/work experience.
Learn prep, line cooking, inventory, costing, sanitation and customer service.
Study bookkeeping, pricing, purchasing, staffing, marketing and licensing.
Develop a concept and business plan; verify local food-service, health and business requirements.

Automotive Technician.summary: Diagnose, repair and maintain cars and light trucks using mechanical and computerized systems.
steps: Consider technical school, community college, manufacturer programs or employer apprenticeship.
Build diagnostic, electrical, brake, engine and computer-scanning skills.
Work toward recognized industry certifications as experience requirements are met.
Join a dealership, independent shop, fleet operation or eventually operate a repair business.

Physical Therapist.summary: Help people restore movement, strength and function after injury or illness.
steps: Complete prerequisite coursework for Doctor of Physical Therapy programs.
Complete an accredited Doctor of Physical Therapy program and clinical rotations.
Pass required national/state examinations and satisfy state licensing rules.
Work in hospitals, outpatient clinics, schools, sports medicine, home care or specialty practice.

Plumber.summary: Install, repair and maintain water, drainage and piping systems in homes, businesses and construction projects.
steps: Pursue a registered apprenticeship or approved employer/union training route with paid on-the-job learning.
Complete required training hours and state or local licensing examinations where required.
Develop strong service, code, troubleshooting, estimating and customer-communication skills.
With experience and proper licensing, explore estimating, insurance, bookkeeping and owning a plumbing company.

Business Administration / Manager.summary: Plan, organize and lead people, budgets and operations so an organization can reach its goals.
steps: Explore business administration, management, accounting, marketing or related college and certificate pathways.
Seek internships, part-time work, clubs or projects that build leadership and customer-service experience.
Learn budgeting, spreadsheets, project management, hiring, communication and data-informed decision making.
Begin in an entry-level business role and grow toward supervision, operations, department leadership or entrepreneurship.

Carpenter.summary: Build, install and repair structures and finishes using wood and other construction materials.
steps: Consider a registered apprenticeship, technical program or supervised employer training route.
Develop framing, finish carpentry, blueprint reading, layout, installation and job-site safety skills.
Build a strong work record and learn estimating, scheduling, codes and customer service.
With experience, explore specialty work, foreperson roles, contracting requirements and business ownership.

Graphic Designer.summary: Create visual communications for print, digital media, brands, campaigns, products and organizations.
steps: Explore graphic design, visual communication, digital media or related college/certificate programs.
Create strong examples of logos, layouts, posters, social media, web and motion/digital design.
Seek school projects, internships, freelance assignments and real-client work while learning feedback and deadlines.
Apply for junior design roles, agency/in-house positions or build a freelance design practice.

Neurosurgeon.summary: Diagnose and surgically treat complex conditions affecting the brain, spine and nervous system.
steps: Typically, earn a bachelor’s degree and complete medical-school admission requirements. No single undergraduate major is required; plan science preparation with an academic adviser.
Complete an MD or DO program, including supervised clinical training. Admission is competitive and preparation does not guarantee acceptance.
Complete specialized neurosurgery residency after medical school. This is an extended period of supervised clinical and surgical training.
Meet medical licensing requirements, including the required examinations. Further fellowship training may support subspecialization; board certification is distinct from state licensure.

Cybersecurity Specialist.summary: Protect computers, networks and information from attacks, misuse and security failures.
steps: A computing-related bachelor’s degree is a common route. Some people enter through relevant industry training and certifications; employer requirements vary.
Develop skills in operating systems, networking and troubleshooting through authorized labs and relevant IT work. Related experience often helps with security roles.
Compare certifications with the requirements of roles that interest you. Employers may prefer them, but no single certification guarantees employment.
Use your training and experience to pursue suitable security roles. Continue developing your knowledge as systems, threats and defensive practices change.

Data Scientist / AI Specialist.summary: Use statistics, programming and machine learning to find patterns in data and build useful predictive or AI systems.
steps: Explore data science, statistics, computer science, mathematics, engineering or related college pathways.
Learn Python, SQL, statistics, data visualization, machine learning and responsible AI practices.
Build projects using public or authorized data and explain both the method and business/social value.
Seek internships and analyst/data roles; continue developing specialty expertise as tools change.

Dental Hygienist.summary: Provide preventive oral-health care, clean teeth, assess patients and teach healthy dental habits.
steps: Complete an accredited dental hygiene education program and required clinical experiences.
Pass the examinations and satisfy the licensing requirements for the state where you plan to work.
Develop strong patient-care, prevention, documentation and teamwork skills in clinical settings.
Work in dental practices, public-health settings or other approved oral-health roles.

Doctor / Physician.summary: Diagnose illness, provide treatment and guide patients in maintaining or restoring health.
steps: Complete a bachelor's degree and pre-medical requirements while gaining healthcare, research or service experience.
Complete an accredited MD or DO program and required licensing examinations.
Train in a chosen specialty through a supervised residency; some specialties require fellowship training.
Complete licensing/credentialing requirements and practice in hospitals, clinics, academic medicine or other settings.

HVAC Technician.summary: Install, maintain and repair heating, ventilation, air-conditioning and refrigeration systems.
steps: Explore technical school, community college, apprenticeship or employer-based HVAC training.
Earn required refrigerant-handling and other applicable certifications and licenses.
Build diagnostic, electrical, airflow, controls and customer-service skills.
Advance into commercial systems, controls, estimating, supervision or properly licensed business ownership.

Lawyer / Attorney.summary: Advise clients, interpret laws, research issues and advocate in negotiations, transactions or court proceedings.
steps: Complete a bachelor's degree in a field that develops strong reasoning, research and communication skills.
Complete an accredited law degree program and gain practical experience through clinics, internships or summer work.
Meet character-and-fitness and bar-examination requirements for the jurisdiction where you plan to practice.
Begin in a firm, government, nonprofit, corporate legal department or another legal setting and build specialty expertise.

Marketing / Advertising Professional.summary: Connect products, services and causes with audiences through research, strategy, storytelling and campaigns.
steps: Explore marketing, business, communications, advertising, analytics or related college/certificate programs.
Create campaigns, social content, research projects and measurable examples of audience growth or engagement.
Seek internships, school organizations, local businesses or nonprofit projects to learn real deadlines and clients.
Apply for marketing coordinator, content, digital, account or analytics roles and develop a specialty.

Medical & Health Services Manager.summary: Lead the business and operational side of healthcare organizations, departments and services.
steps: Explore healthcare administration, business, public health or related bachelor's programs; some roles value graduate study.
Seek healthcare, office, customer-service, internship or project-management experience.
Learn budgeting, compliance, staffing, data, quality improvement and healthcare operations.
Begin in healthcare administration or operations and advance toward department or facility leadership.

Nurse Practitioner.summary: Provide advanced nursing care, assess patients and diagnose and manage many health conditions within state scope-of-practice rules.
steps: Complete an approved nursing program that prepares you for RN licensure, such as a BSN or an associate nursing degree. Pre-nursing prerequisites alone do not qualify you as an RN.
Pass the NCLEX-RN and meet state RN requirements. Compare graduate NP admission requirements; bridge programs may be available for RNs without a BSN.
Complete an appropriate graduate NP program, at the master's or doctoral level, including supervised clinical preparation for your chosen patient population.
Meet national NP certification and state advanced-practice licensing requirements before practicing in that role. Requirements depend on the state and specialty.

Occupational Therapist.summary: Help people develop or regain the everyday skills they need for school, work, home and independent living.
steps: Complete bachelor's-level prerequisites for an accredited occupational therapy graduate program.
Complete an accredited occupational therapy graduate program and required fieldwork.
Meet national certification and state licensing requirements.
Work in hospitals, schools, rehabilitation, pediatrics, mental health, home care or specialty practice.

Physician Assistant.summary: Provide medical care on healthcare teams by evaluating patients, diagnosing conditions and helping manage treatment.
steps: Complete a bachelor's degree and the science/experience prerequisites required by PA programs.
Complete an accredited physician-assistant graduate program and supervised clinical rotations.
Pass required national certification and meet state licensing requirements.
Work in primary care, hospitals, surgery, emergency medicine or a specialty and maintain continuing education.

School Counselor / Mental Health Counsel.summary: Support people with academic, career, social-emotional or mental-health goals through counseling and guidance.
steps: Compare school counseling with clinical mental-health counseling. Their graduate programs, supervised practice and state credentials differ.
Complete relevant undergraduate preparation and a graduate program appropriate to the counseling role and jurisdiction you choose.
Meet the supervised experience and certification or licensing requirements for that role before independent practice.
Seek positions matching your qualifications and continue professional learning and supervision as required.

Web / Digital Designer.summary: Design useful, attractive websites and digital experiences by combining visual design, user needs and technology.
steps: Explore web design, UX/UI, digital media, graphic design or front-end development pathways.
Learn layout, accessibility, responsive design, prototyping, HTML/CSS basics and user-centered design.
Create several polished websites or app prototypes and explain the design decisions behind them.
Apply for junior web, UI/UX or digital-design roles or begin carefully scoped freelance work.

Welder / Fabricator.summary: Join and shape metal to build, repair and manufacture structures, equipment and products.
steps: Explore technical school, community college, apprenticeship or employer welding programs.
Practice appropriate welding processes, cutting, fabrication, inspection and safe equipment use.
Earn employer- or industry-recognized qualifications needed for the type of welding you want to do.
Work in construction, manufacturing, shipbuilding, repair or specialty fabrication and continue developing advanced skills.

Engineer.summary: Use math, science and design to solve practical problems and create systems, products, structures or technology.
steps: Explore an accredited engineering program in a field such as mechanical, civil, electrical, chemical or biomedical engineering.
Join design teams, labs, competitions, co-ops or internships and build evidence of hands-on problem solving.
Learn whether your specialty benefits from or requires engineering-in-training and professional licensure steps.
Begin as an entry-level engineer, develop technical expertise and grow toward project or team leadership.

Accountant / Financial Manager.summary: Help people and organizations understand money, budgets, reporting, controls and financial decisions.
steps: Explore accounting, finance or business degree pathways and understand credential requirements for your goals.
Seek internships or entry-level work involving bookkeeping, budgeting, audit, tax, banking or financial analysis.
For accounting roles that require or value CPA licensure, verify the education, exam and experience rules in your state.
Start in accounting or finance and grow toward senior analyst, controller, financial manager or advisory roles.

Entrepreneur / Business Owner.summary: Create and grow a business by solving a customer problem, managing money and leading day-to-day operations.
steps: Gain real work experience in the field where you might eventually start a business.
Learn pricing, bookkeeping, taxes, insurance, marketing, sales, customer service and hiring basics.
Research customers and competitors, estimate startup costs and test a small version before taking large risks.
Create a realistic business plan, meet legal/licensing requirements, track cash flow and grow carefully.

Special Education Teacher.summary: Help students with disabilities learn, build independence and reach individualized academic, social and transition goals.
steps: Typical coursework: exceptional learners, IEP development, assessment, behavior supports, assistive technology, literacy/numeracy interventions, inclusive instruction, collaboration and special-education law/ethics.
Complete supervised field placements and student teaching with students who have varied learning and support needs.
Complete an approved special-education teacher-preparation program and meet state certification/endorsement requirements.
Begin in resource, inclusion, life-skills or other special-education settings and continue specialty training.

Military / Armed Forces.summary: Serve in one of the U.S. Armed Forces in a military specialty that may involve leadership, technology, logistics, medicine, engineering, aviation, communications or other fields.
steps: Enlisted route: basic training plus a job-specific technical school. Officer routes may include college + ROTC, a service academy or Officer Candidate/Training School. Technical curriculum depends on specialty: aviation, cyber, logistics, medicine, intelligence, engineering and more.
Research branches and specialties carefully, compare service commitments/benefits and speak with family, counselors, veterans and official recruiters before deciding.
Meet service eligibility, testing, medical/fitness and training requirements; some specialties also provide civilian-recognized technical credentials.
Enter an enlisted specialty or commissioning path and deliberately track civilian-transferable skills, education and certifications.

Customer Service Representative.summary: Help customers solve problems, understand products or services, and have a positive experience with a business or organization.
steps: Common training topics: customer communication, de-escalation, product/service knowledge, CRM software, data entry, business writing, privacy/security and problem resolution. College is not always required.
Use retail, hospitality, office, school-help-desk or volunteer roles to practice solving problems for real people.
No universal license; role-specific product, software or industry certifications may help.
Begin in customer service/support and progress into senior support, quality, training, sales, operations or supervision.

Elected Official / Politician.summary: Represent a community in public office by listening to constituents, studying issues, building coalitions and helping shape laws, budgets and policy.
steps: Common useful college study includes political science, public policy, economics, communications or law, with courses such as American government, constitutional law, public policy, statistics, economics and public speaking. A specific degree is not legally required for elected office.
Volunteer on campaigns/community boards, attend public meetings, organize around an issue and learn constituent communication.
Eligibility rules depend on the office and jurisdiction; credibility comes from community involvement, knowledge, ethics and leadership.
Begin with community/campaign service, appointed boards or local office and build a public record before seeking larger roles.

Caregiver / Personal Care Aide.summary: Support older adults or people with disabilities with daily living, safety, companionship and independence in homes or care settings.
steps: Typical training: personal care, infection control, mobility/transfers, nutrition, dementia/disability support, communication, documentation, emergency response and client rights. CNA/HHA training may be useful or required for certain roles/settings.
Build supervised experience helping people with daily participation, independence and social/emotional support.
Requirements vary by job and setting; CPR/first aid and CNA/HHA or agency training may be required.
Work in home care, assisted living, disability support, senior care or community programs and build specialty credentials.

Construction Manager.summary: Plan and coordinate construction projects by managing schedules, budgets, safety, contractors, materials, quality and communication.
steps: Typical coursework: construction methods/materials, estimating, scheduling, contracts, safety, blueprint reading/BIM, cost control, project management, accounting and field operations.
Pursue construction-site internships/co-ops and learn how superintendents, trades, designers, owners and inspectors coordinate.
A bachelor’s degree is common for management-track roles; industry safety/project credentials can strengthen advancement.
Begin as project engineer/assistant PM/field coordinator and progress toward project manager or superintendent.

Psychologist.summary: Study behavior and mental processes and, depending on specialty and licensure, assess, research or help people improve mental health and functioning.
steps: Typical undergraduate psychology: developmental, abnormal, social, cognitive and biological psychology, research methods and statistics. Clinical/counseling graduate study adds assessment, psychotherapy, ethics, advanced research, practicum and internship.
Build research/helping experience; clinical psychologists complete extensive supervised practicum/internship training.
Independent clinical psychologist practice typically requires a doctoral degree, supervised experience, examination and state licensure; other psychology careers have different requirements.
Work in clinical, school, research, organizational or community settings depending on degree/credential path.
